title: Isolation ledger of a2dlc run (.a2dlc/run/<slice>/ledger.json, not committed)
description: One entry per launch of a role, append-only and chained: hash = sha256(prev_hash + canonical JSON of the entry without hash). It attests what each role saw (inputs mounted with their hash), what it left (outputs), with which image and command, with which network and which variable names. The negative attestation (the Saboteur did not see the Builder's code) holds because the only one that launches containers is the core. a2dlc verify-run recomputes the chain. Limit: it records the declared family and what the CLI reported, not which model answered.

prev_hash.description: null only in the first entry.

role.description: A launched role, or `check` in the entry that binds one use of an authorization: it launches nothing (family script, network none, no cost) and carries `authorization`.

image_digest.description: docker image inspect; null if the image is local without a digest.

argv_sha256.description: The full argv of docker run, mounts included: this way the record also proves what was NOT mounted.

network.description: Network the role launch had, as the launcher reports it: none (roles.json network none or absent) or proxy-allowlist (roles.json network provider: egress goes through the allowlist proxy). provider and bridge-unrestricted stay in the enum for ledgers written before the egress proxy; the launcher no longer produces them.

env_keys.description: Names of the variables in the env_file. Never values.

egress_proxy.description: The egress proxy image that filtered this launch, present only when network is proxy-allowlist (absent in ledgers written before it). image is the tag the launcher asked for; image_digest identifies the content the proxy ran from: the repo digest when the image has one, else the image ID of a local build.

authorization.description: Only in an entry of role check: the chained binding of one record of authorizations_used, which has the same stage and at. id is the sha256 of the authorization's signed text (what the receipt calls its id); sha256 is the sha256 of the record's `authorization` object (keys in the order of authorization.schema.json, no spaces, signature included).

authorizations_used.description: RFC-0007 Part B. One record per waived target that a run let pass because a signed authorization (.a2dlc/authorizations.json) covered it instead of stopping for an approval: the stage whose check relied on it, the time of use, the target and the whole signed authorization. a2dlc verify-run checks each record again against the allowed signers (never the repo): the signature in namespace a2dlc-authorization, the target among the authorization's, and expires_at not passed at `at`. Each record is bound into the hash chain by exactly one entry of role check (its `authorization`, same stage and at), so deleting or editing a record breaks verify-run's chain check. Limit: the chain has no anchor outside the folder, so removing the last entries of the chain together with their records is not detected.
